parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files serve one concern: delivery and persistence adapters for the task-management application. `server.ts` starts the app, `app.ts` is the Express HTTP adapter, and `inMemoryRepositories.ts` implements the domain repository interfaces (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository). That part is cohesive and uses the module's abstractions properly: `createApp` wires the in-memory repositories into TaskManagementService.

The problem is in `app.ts`, which copies a domain rule instead of keeping it in one place. In two handlers (POST and GET /projects/:projectId/tasks) it repeats the same `isTaskStatus` check and writes out the allowed statuses as the literal string "status must be one of todo, in_progress, done". The domain already owns that set through `isTaskStatus`, so the handler's message is a third, hand-written copy that will go stale if a status is added.

`app.ts` also checks inputs unevenly. The POST tasks handler checks `assigneeId` itself ("assigneeId must be a string"). PUT /tasks/:taskId/assignee passes `body(req).assigneeId` to `svc.assignTask` unchecked. And `title`, `description` and `dueDate` go to `svc.addTask` as unknown values. This suggests the service already validates its inputs, so the adapter partly repeats that validation and is inconsistent about which inputs it checks. This is an inference, because the service source isn't in the material. The duplication is small but concrete, so I'm failing the unit at moderate confidence.

The domain already owns this set through `isTaskStatus`, so the rule should live in one place (the domain or one shared helper).

Validation is inconsistent across handlers: assigneeId is checked in POST /projects/:projectId/tasks but not in PUT /tasks/:taskId/assignee, and other fields go to the service unchecked. This partly repeats validation the service appears to own.
